options.text: At a meeting point of an arc from $G$ of radius $7\,\mathrm{cm}$ and an arc from $H$ of radius $6\,\mathrm{cm}$.
Anywhere on the dashed arc drawn from $G$, because that arc is labelled first.
On the midpoint of segment $GH$, because $GH$ is the drawn base.
At endpoint $H$, because $H$ already sits on the base.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Rohan looks at the diagram. He has drawn base $GH$ of length $8\,\mathrm{cm}$. He must build triangle $GHI$ with $GI = 7\,\mathrm{cm}$ and $HI = 6\,\mathrm{cm}$.

part_answers.answer: Point $I$ must be $7\,\mathrm{cm}$ from $G$ and $6\,\mathrm{cm}$ from $H$, so it lies at an intersection of those two arcs.

teacher.key_rationale: The third vertex is the intersection of arcs with radii equal to the remaining sides. Using only one arc omits the second radius. The midpoint and endpoint grab base features.
teacher.figure_note: Rewritten base GH with two construction arcs.
